newsitem.title: USA: Compaq Computer profits up 43 percent.
newsitem.headline: Compaq Computer profits up 43 percent.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp. said Wednesday its profits jumped 43 percent in the third quarter as it increased sales of personal computers and accessories and streamlined operations.

Compaq, the largest supplier of personal computers in the world, said its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 soared to $350 million, or $1.26 a share, from $245 million, or 89 cents a share.
The per-share results were well above Wall Street estimates of $1.07, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
However, the company's stock dropped $1.875 to $73.25 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Houston-based company, which had worldwide sales of $14.8 billion last year, said its revenues expanded by 25 percent in the quarter, to $4.5 billion from $3.6 billion.
Compaq said its accessories business, which includes monitors, hard drives, keyboards, and CD changers, grew significantly over the third quarter and remained one of its most profitable segments.

The company said its net income for the first nine months of the year grew by 20 percent to $851 million, or $3.07 a share, from $707 million, or $2.59 a share. Revenues rose to $12.7 billion from $10.1 billion.
